MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 8, 2019

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Raths at 5:00 p.m., on January 8, 2019, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 3, 2019, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
  Mayor Raths

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Raths recessed the meeting. The City Council reconvened at 6:02
p.m. with all five Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Council Member Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Presentation to Former Mayor Sachs

City Council Minutes  1  January 8, 2019
   Mayor Raths presented Council Member Sachs with a gavel plaque for his service as
  Mayor in 2018.

P2.  Opening Remarks from Mayor Raths

  Mayor Raths presented his goals for the year. He also presented a Certificate of
  Appreciation to Michael Joseph Maiolo for his bravery in assisting Mission Viejo Police
  Services with an arrest and named SoulScale and Rescom Financial Services as Business
  and Community Partners.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Robert Breton, M.V.: saluted former Mayor Ed Sachs for representing and presiding over the city
as Mayor in 2018 in a dignified and statesman-like manner.

Bob Hayes, M.V.: discussed the Mission Viejo Community of Character program and announced
that the character trait for the month of January is perseverance.

Bruce Teel, M.V.: expressed his concern with the proposal to raise the Council stipend by 62.5%
at the October 23, 2018, City Council meeting. He asked the Council to reject the proposal if it
ever comes up again.

Dale Rathburn, M.V.: spoke about a residential drug and rehab facility that opened next door to
his home. He cited several ways in which the owners are operating outside of the law and he asked
the City for help.

Mahmoud El-Farra, M.V.: announced that it would be a privilege to serve on any of Mission
Viejo’s commissions or committees to work with others toward a common goal.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of December 11, 2018, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated November 30, 2018 in the Amount of $451,962.28

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  2  January 8, 2019
 3.  Check Register dated December 7, 2018 in the amount of $1,061,519.17

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Fiscal Year 2017-18 Mission Viejo Housing Authority Annual Report

  Received and filed.

5.  Review and Approval of Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule for the 19-20 A-B
  Annual Fiscal Period of July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020

  (1) Adopted Successor Agency Resolution No. 19-01 Approving the Recognized
  Obligation Payment Schedule 19-20 A-B for the Annual Fiscal period of July 1, 2019 to
  June 30, 2020, Subject to Submittal to and Review by the Orange Countywide Oversight
  Board and by the Department of Finance Under the Division 24, Part 1.85 of the California
  Health and Safety Code, and Authorizing the Posting and Transmittal Thereof; and (2)
  further, the Director of Administrative Services, in consultation with legal counsel, was
  authorized to request and complete meet and confer session(s), if any, with the Department
  of Finance and authorized to make augmentations, modifications, additions or revisions as
  may be necessary or directed by the Department of Finance.

6.  Christopher Park Play Area - CIP (312)

  (1) Awarded a contract for Christopher Park Play Area design services and preparation of
  construction drawings to Richard Fischer Associates in an amount not to exceed
  $39,125.00; (2) adopted Resolution 19-01 Amending the Current FY 2018/19 Operating
  Budget in the amount of $100,000.

7.  Purchase Replacement Cardio Equipment for the Montanoso Recreation Center and
  Sierra Recreation Center

  Approved the purchase agreement for the replacement of cardio equipment for the
  Montanoso Recreation Center and Sierra Recreation Center in the amount of $47,500.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

OLD BUSINESS

8.  Dissolution of Supplemental Health Account for Retired Employees Plan Board of
  Trustees

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  approve dissolution of Supplemental Health Account for Retired Employees Plan Board of
  Trustees.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  3  January 8, 2019
   AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

9.  Appointment of City Commission Members

  Planning and Transportation Commission

  Council Member Bucknum nominated Cameron Knauerhaze, Council Member Kelley
  nominated Robert Breton, Council Member Sachs nominated Robert Ruesch, Mayor Pro
  Tem Goodell nominated Joseph Blum and Mayor Raths nominated Dave Leckness.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  approve the five Planning and Transportation Commission appointments.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Community Services Commission

  Council Member Bucknum nominated Pam Smith, Council Member Kelley nominated
  Cathy Allen, Council Member Sachs nominated Debbie Ruesch, Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  4  January 8, 2019
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

10. City Council Committee and Regional Board/Committee  Representative
  Appointments and Update Posting of FPPC Form 806 Online

  Mayor Raths appointed Ed Sachs to serve on the Orange County Fire Authority Board of

  Motion made by Mayor Raths, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
  appointment of Ed Sachs to represent Mission Viejo on the Orange County Fire Authority
  Board of Directors.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Mayor Raths appointed Trish Kelley to serve as representative and Brian Goodell to serve
  as alternate on the Transportation Corridor Agencies Board of Directors.

  Motion made by Mayor Raths, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
  appointment of Trish Kelley as representative and Brian Goodell as alternate on the
  Transportation Corridor Agencies Board of Directors.

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, and Raths

  (e) Voter Education Ad Hoc Committee –Trish Kelley and Greg Raths

  (a) California Joint Powers Insurance Authority – Ed Sachs/Chery Dyas
  (b) League of California Cities and Association of California Cities, Orange County – Greg
  Raths/Brian Goodell
  (c) Orange County Council of Governments General Assembly – Brian Goodell/Trish Kelley

City Council Minutes  5  January 8, 2019
   (d) Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) General Assembly – Wendy
  Bucknum/Trish Kelley
  (e) Southern Orange County Watershed Management Area Executive Committee – Trish
  Kelley/Brian Goodell

  The City Clerk was directed to update the appointees list as required by law on Form 806
  and post the form to the City’s website.

STAFF REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

11.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum wished residents a very happy New Year. She discussed yesterday’s
swearing-in ceremonies for several county officials, including the new Orange County Sheriff,
Don Barnes. She said it was an absolute honor to attend that ceremony. In addition, several new
County Board Members were sworn in as was the new District Attorney. Council Member
Bucknum encouraged residents to attend the upcoming character movie, The Blind Side, which,
she said, is a great representation of perseverance. In closing, Council Member Bucknum stated that
she is looking forward to working cooperatively with the new Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem this year.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley said it was a wonderful holiday season and she had a very enjoyable time
with family. She noted that her grandkids are back in school now and it has been a relatively quiet
last two weeks. She announced that she too attended the swearing-in ceremony for the new Sheriff,
Don Barnes, and stated that the County is fortunate to have a man of such integrity and talent.
Council Member Kelley said she really valued former Sheriff Hutchens and is glad to see that the
baton has been passed to such a good person. She thanked Bob Hayes from the Character
Committee for speaking at the beginning of the meeting about this month’s character quality,
perseverance. The character movie will be shown Sunday, January 20 at 2:00 pm in the Council
Chamber. Attendance is free and the movie will be followed by a discussion of the character
quality. In conclusion, Council Member Kelley read a quote from the poem The Race, written by
D.H. Groberg: “For all of life is like that race, with ups and downs and all. And all you have to do
to win is rise each time you fall.”

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs outlined last evening’s Town Hall Meeting which addressed rising San
Diego Gas and Electric (SDG&E) rates. He noted that about 80% of the Chamber was filled with
SDG&E customers and there were two representatives from SDG&E present, with the Vice
President of Customer Service responding to questions. Council Member Sachs said the SDG&E
City Council Minutes  6  January 8, 2019
 representative was ill-prepared for the meeting, did not take the residents seriously, and he learned
during the discussion that residents are treated like little children when they call SDG&E with
questions and concerns. Several times during the meeting, the Vice President responded to
questions by saying that the answer might be too complicated for residents to understand. Council
Member Sachs stated that Mission Viejo residents don’t have a choice for their electric service and
the voice of the community is not being heard or taken seriously. He said the SDG&E
representative almost bragged that they are the most expensive utility company in over 90% of the
country and he tap danced around many questions. Council Member Sachs noted that it is well
documented that if a city leaves a utility company, there is an onerous disconnect fee and the city
would still have to use the power grid. So, he said, the answers are not very good when looking
down the road. Council Member Sachs said some residents reported they now have to make
decisions as to whether they pay their electric bill and how much grocery shopping they can do.
He vowed to continue working towards solutions to the exorbitant electricity rates.

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell announced that he received an email from a group called Public
Watchdogs regarding the Nuclear Regulatory Commission’s disposal of used fuel at San Onofre
Nuclear Generating Station. The email announced that there will be a webcast tomorrow at 10:00
a.m. and information is available on the Public Watchdogs website. He said it will be very
interesting to hear about the plan to dispose of the nuclear waste. Council Member Goodell noted
that he has the webcast information and can share it with members of the audience tonight or
residents can email him at bgoodell@cityofmissionviejo.org. He said it was also called to his
attention that there have already been a couple of near misses with waste storage at San Onofre
that were not publicly disclosed per the law. Council Member Goodell thanked his colleagues for
selecting him as Mayor Pro Tem for the year and said he is looking forward to getting some things
done. He thanked Ed Sachs for a job well done in leading the Council with distinction as the 2018
Mayor.

Mayor Raths

12.  Appointment of Mission Viejo City Ambassador

  Mayor Raths presented his report.

  Council Member Bucknum stated that she thinks the resolution needs some work and
  should be tightened up. She said there are some redundancies and the resolution should
  describe exactly what the Ambassador does that the City Council does not do.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, to table
  this matter to the next meeting to allow time for the resolution to be tightened up.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  7  January 8, 2019
   Mayor Raths asked Council Member Bucknum to work with City Attorney Curley on the
  resolution language.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:18 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Raths adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, January 22, 2019, at 5:00 p.m.
